items.title: Democrats' midterm sweep redraws map of state power
items.feedTitle: Democratic thrashing redraws the map of state power
items.summary: Republicans lost control of state legislatures and executive offices across historically red states following Democratic victories in the 2026 midterms. The shift signals a major realignment of political power at the state level, with implications for education, healthcare, and other policy areas. Democrats now control more statewide positions than they have in recent decades, potentially reshaping governance in Texas, Georgia, Kansas, and other key states.

items.title: Voters demanded economic relief; Trump and Democrats face tough choices
items.feedTitle: Voters demanded economic relief. Trump and Democrats face tough choices on how to deliver
items.summary: The 2026 midterm results reflected strong voter demand for action on cost of living, inflation, and economic security. Both the Trump administration and incoming Democratic Congress face pressure to deliver tangible relief on housing, healthcare, and everyday expenses. However, economists and policymakers differ sharply on what policies will actually reduce costs without creating new problems.

items.title: Midterm results deliver 'youth quake' to American politics
items.feedTitle: Midterm results deliver ‘youth quake’ to American politics
items.summary: The 2026 midterm elections saw a notably younger cohort of candidates elected across the country, from James Talarico in Texas to Gina Hinojosa and others in competitive races. Younger Democrats, in particular, displaced senior incumbents and brought fresh energy to Congress. This generational shift could influence policy priorities and legislative style over the next decade.

items.title: Trump appoints hardliner Stephen Miller as White House chief of staff
items.feedTitle: What Trump picking Stephen Miller for chief of staff signals about his agenda
items.summary: President Trump promoted Stephen Miller, the architect of his hardline immigration agenda, to chief of staff following the Republican midterm defeat. Miller replaces Susie Wiles and signals Trump's intention to double down on immigration restrictions and mass deportations despite electoral losses tied to immigration concerns. Immigration officials say ICE is unlikely to scale back operations under Miller's leadership.

items.title: House Democrats prepare to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth
items.feedTitle: House poised to impeach Pete Hegseth after GOP midterm defeat
items.summary: Following Republican losses in the midterms, House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries and other top Democrats signaled they are prepared to move forward with impeachment proceedings against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. Democrats cite concerns about his management record and controversial statements. The move reflects deepening divisions between the Democratic Congress and Trump administration.

stlouis.title: SLU defeats Missouri 90-84 in renewed Show Me Showdown rivalry
stlouis.feedTitle: SLU rises to the challenge, beats Missouri 90-84 as rivalry gets restarted
stlouis.summary: Saint Louis University's Billikens defeated the University of Missouri Tigers 90-84 in a restart of their historic basketball rivalry after years apart. McCottry and Sharma each scored 17 points, and SLU made 14 three-pointers to overcome Missouri. The win marks the first matchup in the revived Show Me Showdown series between the two St. Louis area schools.

stlouis.title: St. Louis City SC earns No. 3 seed in MLS Playoffs
stlouis.feedTitle: St. Louis City SC earns No. 3 seed in playoffs with 1-0 win
stlouis.summary: St. Louis City SC secured the third seed in the MLS Playoffs with a 1-0 victory, extending their strong season performance. The win positions the team favorably for the postseason tournament. City SC's playoff seeding reflects a competitive 2026 regular season in Major League Soccer.

stlouis.title: St. Louis County corrects property tax billing errors, bills restored online
stlouis.feedTitle: Corrected St. Louis County property tax bills back online after errors, county says
stlouis.summary: St. Louis County announced that corrected property tax bills have been restored to online systems following a period of errors and inaccessibility. The county acknowledged problems with the billing portal and has now made corrected statements available for residents. County officials attributed the issues to technical problems in the tax billing system.

items.title: Houthi missiles strike Saudi Aramco building in Riyadh financial hub
items.feedTitle: Saudi Aramco Tower Damaged as Yemen’s Houthis Attack Riyadh
items.summary: Yemen's Houthi militant group claimed responsibility for missile attacks on Riyadh's financial district, damaging a building belonging to Saudi oil giant Aramco. The attack represents an escalation in regional tensions and the ongoing conflict in Yemen. Saudi Arabia has not yet publicly responded to the strike, though the incident comes amid broader US-Iran military tensions.

items.title: Israel's president names opposition leader Eisenkot to form government
items.feedTitle: Israel’s president picks Yashar leader Gadi Eisenkot to form government
items.summary: Israeli President Isaac Herzog tasked opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot, a former military chief and Netanyahu's rival, with forming the next government after the deadlocked election left neither Netanyahu's bloc nor opposition with a clear majority. Eisenkot has 28 days to assemble a ruling coalition. The appointment is seen as a setback for Netanyahu, who has dominated Israeli politics for years.

items.title: Two trains collide in Egypt, at least four killed near Cairo
items.feedTitle: Collision of two trains in Egypt kills at least four
items.summary: Two trains collided near Cairo in al-Ayyat, killing at least four people and injuring nearly 90 others. One train derailed following the collision south of the Egyptian capital. President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi ordered a prompt investigation into the accident. The incident raises concerns about rail safety and maintenance standards on Egypt's heavily-used rail network.

items.title: Russian strikes on Ukraine knock out hundreds of thousands without power
items.feedTitle: Russian strikes on Ukraine leave hundreds of thousands without electricity
items.summary: Russian missile and drone attacks on Ukraine's energy infrastructure left about 850,000 people without electricity in the Dnipropetrovsk and Kharkiv regions. The strikes targeted civilian power plants and water systems ahead of trilateral peace talks scheduled for Abu Dhabi. Ukraine's military said the attacks were designed to pressure negotiating positions before discussions with Russian and US delegations.

items.title: Anuj Shrivatri becomes India's 100th Chess Grandmaster
items.feedTitle: Anuj Shrivatri becomes India's 100th Grandmaster, Madhya Pradesh's first
items.summary: Anuj Shrivatri achieved a historic milestone, becoming India's 100th Grandmaster and the first from Madhya Pradesh. The accomplishment marks a significant achievement for Indian chess, reflecting the country's growing strength in the sport. Shrivatri's elevation comes as India continues to produce world-class chess talent.

items.title: India basks in Diwali fervour, but Delhi's smog casts a shadow over celebrations

items.title: Oil India facility fire in Assam death toll rises to four
items.feedTitle: Death toll in Oil India facility in Assam rises to four as another injured dies
items.summary: The death toll from a fire at an Oil India Limited facility in Assam climbed to four as another injured worker succumbed to injuries. The incident raised serious questions about workplace safety at the oil production facility. OIL has instituted a high-level inquiry into the accident and suspended four officials pending investigation.

items.title: Portion of false ceiling collapses at Mumbai airport terminal 2
items.feedTitle: Portion of false ceiling collapses outside Mumbai airport terminal, one hurt
items.summary: A section of false ceiling collapsed outside Mumbai's airport terminal 2, injuring one person. The airport's emergency medical team immediately responded to provide first aid. The incident raises concerns about maintenance and structural integrity at the busy international airport terminal.

items.title: PM Modi celebrates Diwali with security forces in Bastar region
items.feedTitle: ‘First Diwali when every district of India is free from Naxalism’: PM Modi in Bastar
items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi spent Diwali with CRPF and CoBRA personnel in Bastar, Chhattisgarh, marking what he called the 'first Diwali when every district of India is free from Naxalism.' Modi used the occasion to target ideological opponents, warning of 'Dimagi Naxals' he says have 'infiltrated' political parties. The visit highlighted security operations and counterinsurgency efforts in the region.

immigration.title: DHS ends automatic extension of employment authorization documents
immigration.feedTitle: Removal of Automatic Extensions for Certain Employment Authorization Documents
immigration.summary: The Department of Homeland Security published an interim final rule ending the automatic extension of validity for Forms I-766 (Employment Authorization Documents/EADs) for applicants who timely filed renewal applications. Under the new rule, finalized and in effect as of late October 2025, affected workers will need to ensure their renewals are processed before current authorizations expire. This affects employment-based visa holders including H-1B dependents and other temporary visa categories.

immigration.title: US green card backlog exceeds 1.56 million applications
immigration.feedTitle: More than 1.56 million US green card applications face backlog
immigration.summary: USCIS data shows more than 1.56 million pending green card applications, with family-based cases accounting for 611,000 and employment-based cases for 268,000. The backlog reflects systemic delays in visa processing and adjudication. Proposed, not final—Democrats have indicated they may push for expedited processing, but no binding rule changes have been announced. The backlog particularly affects Indian nationals in the EB-2 category.

immigration.title: Democrats' midterm control could reshape H-1B visa policy
immigration.feedTitle: Can Democrats reverse Trump's H-1B policies? What US midterms mean for immigrants
immigration.summary: Following Democratic victories in the 2026 midterms, analysts and immigration advocates suggest potential for policy changes on H-1B visas and employment-based immigration. Democrats have historically favored increasing visa caps and easing restrictions that Trump policies tightened. However, proposed rule changes—not yet final—face implementation hurdles and potential Republican obstruction. India's IT sector is closely watching Democratic Congress for relief on visa curbs.

items.title: Anthropic secures $3.4 billion gas-fired power deal for AI data centers
items.feedTitle: Anthropic secures $3.4 billion generator deal for AI data centers, FT reports
items.summary: Anthropic announced a $3.4 billion investment to purchase 1.7 gigawatts of gas-fired generator capacity from a supplier, securing energy for its expanding AI data center operations. The deal underscores the massive power requirements of large language model training and inference. The commitment represents a significant bet on fossil fuel energy despite climate concerns, signaling the infrastructure demands of the AI boom.

items.title: Indian stock indices end Diwali Muhurat trading in rare red session
items.feedTitle: A rare red Diwali: Sensex ends Muhurat trading lower for only the eighth time in 30 years
items.summary: The Sensex and Nifty ended the 2026 Diwali Muhurat trading session lower, marking only the eighth time in 30 years the auspicious session closed in red. The decline snapped a seven-day winning streak and reflected profit-taking after the rally. Smaller companies and select sectors like pharma and defense were gainers, but broader profit-taking pressure dominated the special session.

items.title: Corporate earnings barely beat Wall Street expectations amid uncertainty
items.feedTitle: Corporate America’s profit numbers are just barely beating Wall Street’s expectations
items.summary: US companies reported third-quarter earnings that only marginally exceeded analyst expectations, raising questions about earnings quality and forward growth. The tepid earnings backdrop comes amid AI sector volatility, geopolitical tensions, and investor concerns about profit sustainability. Market analysts note that companies are delivering on projections but struggling to exceed them by meaningful margins.

items.title: Tesla to wind down Cybertruck production, shift focus to robotics
items.feedTitle: Tesla to wind down Cybertruck production as Elon Musk focuses on robotics and AI
items.summary: Elon Musk announced that Tesla will halt Cybertruck production to redirect the Texas factory toward manufacturing its self-driving Cybercab taxi. The decision marks an effective end to the company's high-profile electric pickup effort, which failed to capture significant market share despite years of development. The pivot reflects Musk's prioritization of autonomous vehicle technology over traditional vehicle platforms.

items.title: US added 165,000 jobs in October despite economic uncertainty
items.feedTitle: US job growth exceeds expectations in October despite economic uncertainty
items.summary: The US labor market added 165,000 jobs in October, and previous month figures were revised upward by a combined 84,000, suggesting resilience despite inflation concerns and Middle East tensions. The "low-hire, low-fire" labor market shows subdued but steady growth. Economists expect the Federal Reserve may continue rate adjustments given the mixed signals from employment and inflation data.

finance.note: US stocks ended the week sharply lower as AI sector volatility and profit-taking dominated trading following the Democratic midterm sweep. Oil prices remain pressured by geopolitical uncertainty over US-Iran tensions and Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure, while Indian markets snapped a seven-day rally with Sensex and Nifty closing lower in rare red Diwali Muhurat trading. Watch: US inflation data next week, Fed rate signals, and developments in Middle East tensions that could further roil commodities and tech valuations.

cards.title: Deep Work Requires Environmental Protection
cards.insight: High-stakes decision-making and complex problem-solving demand uninterrupted focus time. Protecting your environment—whether through physical boundaries, notification management, or time-blocking—is not a luxury but a prerequisite for high-quality output.
cards.takeaway: Schedule 90-minute blocks of uninterrupted work and communicate to colleagues/family that this time is protected.

cards.title: Task Switching Destroys Cognitive Flow
cards.insight: Switching between tasks costs far more than the time it takes to switch. Your brain requires time to re-establish context and momentum. Batch similar tasks together and minimize context-switching throughout the day.
cards.takeaway: Group email, messaging, and administrative work into dedicated windows rather than responding reactively throughout the day.

cards.title: Energy Management Beats Time Management
cards.insight: You cannot optimize time, but you can optimize energy. Cognitive performance peaks at different hours for different people. Identify your peak energy windows and defend them for high-leverage work rather than defaulting to available time slots.
cards.takeaway: Track your energy levels for one week and assign your most important work to your strongest windows.

cards.title: Clear Stopping Points Improve Starting Momentum
cards.insight: Ambiguous or open-ended work sessions create cognitive drag that extends beyond work hours. Defining a clear stopping point—a specific goal, milestone, or time boundary—signals to your brain that the task is complete, freeing mental resources.
cards.takeaway: Start each work session with a specific, measurable endpoint; record it and refer back to it as you near completion.

ai.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Cyber cybersecurity model with 'Critical' rating
ai.feedTitle: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Cyber with ‘Critical’ cybersecurity rating
ai.summary: OpenAI released GPT-6 Cyber, a specialized security model rated as 'Critical' for cybersecurity tasks. The release comes as AI labs face increasing scrutiny over their role in digital infrastructure protection and risk mitigation. OpenAI positioned the model as addressing enterprise security needs, though details on real-world deployment remain limited.

ai.title: Alleged Chinese spy recruitment of Nvidia CEO exposed in intelligence memo
ai.feedTitle: Megaspeed exec was recruited to spy on Nvidia CEO, according to US intelligence memo
ai.summary: A US intelligence memo allegedly revealed that China's Ministry of State Security recruited a female technology executive to spy on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. The allegation surfaced amid broader congressional scrutiny of Nvidia's China business and export control compliance. The incident underscores geopolitical tensions around AI chip supply chains and US-China technology competition.
